directed.conceptual_reading: A marginal Gaussian law can set the scale of typical fluctuations without determining maxima. The independence calculation is useful as a foil: changing only the dependence structure can change the extreme-value regime even when one-point behavior remains Gaussian.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Taking the negative logarithm of the modulus converts multiplicative zeta values into an additive random-potential landscape. That representation makes covariance and statistical-mechanical extreme-value tools available while preserving the locations of maxima as minima of the potential.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This span neither derives the correlation law nor determines the maximum. Its broad bounds and independence baseline do not establish where the true extremes lie, and the split layout of equation (1) should not be used for exact formula recovery.
directed.uncertainty: The independence model is explicitly heuristic, and the exact normalization of its predicted maximum is formula-fragile in this extraction. Confidence is high only in the prose-supported contrast between that baseline and strong correlation.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The source builds a three-way bridge: established zeta/random-matrix statistical analogies identify a surrogate, and the shared logarithmic landscape suggests importing a freezing mechanism. Its sharper target is the full maximum law for one matrix, not merely a tail assembled from many matrices.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The span recalls conjectural asymptotic correspondences between zeta zeros and random-matrix eigenvalues and between zeta values and characteristic polynomials. It then proposes that the low-temperature freezing transition of logarithmically correlated disordered landscapes governs characteristic-polynomial extremes and, conjecturally, zeta extremes, while distinguishing single-matrix maxima from earlier many-matrix tail questions.
directed.conceptual_reading: The proposed transfer is structural rather than based on surface resemblance: match the dependence geometry, identify an extreme-value mechanism in the tractable model, and only then formulate a zeta prediction. Separating the single-object distribution from repeated-sampling tails also prevents two different extremal questions from being conflated.
directed.representation_or_bridge: A CUE characteristic polynomial is the intermediate mathematical object connecting zeta statistics to a random energy landscape. Its log modulus can be treated as an energy field, so matrix size, circle position, and inverse temperature can later be aligned with zeta height, local displacement, and extremal bias.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The span states an analogy and research program, not a proof of transfer to zeta. Existing statistical correspondences are described as believed, rare zeta extremes remain numerically unresolved, and a many-matrix tail result does not by itself give the one-matrix maximum law.
directed.uncertainty: The central freezing claim is explicitly speculative for zeta. The two-column extraction is interleaved, but the scope distinction and conjectural status are clear in the prose.

For each fixed mode these coefficients tend to independent complex Gaussians under CUE averaging. The resulting covariance is stated as -2 log|2 sin((θ_1-θ_2)/2)| in the large-N limit, with its short-distance divergence saturating when the separation is of order N^{-1}.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The maximum is replaced by a temperature-indexed soft minimum: the partition function retains the whole landscape at finite β, while its zero-temperature free energy recovers the extremum. This creates the operative route from a hard maximum problem to freezing.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source defines a partition function by integrating |p_N(θ)|^{2β}, equivalently exp(-β V_N^(U)(θ)), around the circle, and sets F(β)=-β^{-1} log Z_N(β). As β tends to infinity, F(β) tends to min_θ V_N^(U)(θ), which equals -2 max_θ log|p_N(θ)|.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is a variational reframing: a nonsmooth extremum is approached through a family of log-integrals that can be studied by moments and phase-transition methods. Temperature controls how strongly the representation selects deep minima, and freezing predicts when further selection stops changing normalized free energy.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Z_N and F are bridge objects between characteristic-polynomial maxima and statistical mechanics. They preserve the target extremum in the β→∞ limit while exposing intermediate observables that can be compared across CUE, random landscapes, and zeta.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The max/free-energy limit does not establish that freezing occurs, and Gaussian logarithmic covariance alone does not prove the needed partition-function law. Transfer of the resulting mechanism from CUE to zeta remains conjectural.
directed.uncertainty: The semantic roles of the integral, free energy, and zero-temperature limit are explicit. Exact normalizing factors in the fragmented displays should be scan-checked.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The analogy gains mathematical content when integer partition-function moments become Toeplitz determinants and then a Dyson-Morris/Selberg integral. The resulting moment form matches the circular logarithmic model up to scale, providing an actual transfer mechanism.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For positive integer k, the source rewrites moments of Z_N(β) as k-fold circle integrals involving a Toeplitz determinant. Large-N Toeplitz asymptotics produce a product of pairwise angular-distance factors, recognized as a Dyson-Morris version of the Selberg integral, and hence a moment law of the same form as that of a circular logarithmic landscape.
directed.conceptual_reading: The proof strategy changes representation twice to reveal known structure: random-matrix averaging becomes a determinant, and determinant asymptotics become an integrable pair-interaction model. Matching an entire moment law is more constraining than matching a covariance, although it still has a restricted domain.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Toeplitz determinants are the bridge from CUE averages to Selberg integrals; the latter expose the circular log-model partition law. The characteristic scale may change while the functional moment structure, which carries the freezing information, is preserved.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The displayed exponents and convergence threshold are OCR-fragile and are not reconstructed. The moment calculation is subcritical and integer-moment based; divergence outside its domain means that continuation to the frozen phase is not justified by these displayed moments alone.
directed.uncertainty: The prose-supported Toeplitz-to-Selberg reduction and matching-form claim are reliable. Exact constants, powers, and admissible inequalities require scan verification.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Transferring the circular-log moment law yields several linked discriminants, not just a leading scale: a 3/2 log-log centering correction, a modified-Bessel fluctuation density, and a left tail different from the short-range Gumbel model.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Because the CUE partition-function moments have the circular-logarithmic form, the source transfers that model's centered and scaled maximum law. It identifies a conjectural 3/2 coefficient in the log-log correction, a density expressed with a modified Bessel function, and a left tail proportional to |x|e^x, contrasting these with the 1/2 correction and Gumbel behavior expected for short-range correlations.
directed.conceptual_reading: A universality-class claim becomes more falsifiable when it predicts multiple observables. Centering, bulk fluctuation shape, and tail behavior probe different consequences of the same correlation mechanism and can fail separately.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The centered/scaled maximum variable compresses matrix-size dependence into deterministic location and scale terms, leaving a limiting law that can be compared with zeta windows. The circular-log partition law is the bridge that selects this normalization and density.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The transfer and the 3/2 coefficient are conjectural, and the interleaved zeta discussion is preliminary rather than a derivation. Agreement of one normalized distribution would not by itself prove the entire freezing mechanism.
directed.uncertainty: The qualitative Bessel-density identification, 3/2-versus-1/2 contrast, and tail statement are clear in prose. Equations (12)-(14), including exact fractions and scale factors, need scan verification.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The numerical test is organized as a direct competition between correlation models: after mapping a zeta height to an effective CUE size, the observed mean maxima are much closer to the 3/2 correction than to the short-range 1/2 correction.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source computes maxima of |ζ(1/2+it)| on many intervals of length 2π at several heights, takes N near log T, and compares sample means with two model means differing in the centering coefficient c. The displayed ratios are near one for c=3/2 and near one half for c=1/2, leading the authors to report a considerably better fit for the logarithmic-correlation model.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is a competing-model test rather than an absolute goodness claim. The subleading centering term functions as a diagnostic because the two models share much of the leading scale but disagree on a specific consequence of dependence.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Local zeta windows are represented as effective CUE samples through N approximately log T, and division by the model mean turns data from different heights into comparable ratios. That normalization makes the correlation hypothesis visible in a compact table.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The table reports finite-height numerical evidence, not independent validation or a proof of the asymptotic law. The damaged model-mean display is not reconstructed, and the comparison may still be affected by finite-size and arithmetic corrections.
directed.uncertainty: The table entries and the authors' comparative conclusion are readable. Confidence is limited to the reported fit; no independent recomputation or exact formula recovery is available within this packet.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Instead of inferring freezing only from maxima, the source constructs a beta-indexed zeta partition function. This makes the proposed phase transition directly observable through how integrated critical-line mass changes with inverse temperature.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source defines z_β(T) as a normalized integral of |ζ(1/2+iy)|^{2β} over the interval from T to T+2π, explicitly as the zeta analogue of the CUE partition function Z_N(β).
directed.conceptual_reading: The observable enlarges a single extreme statistic into a response curve indexed by β. Small β averages broadly over the interval, whereas large β increasingly selects the largest values, so a freezing transition can be tested as a change in this response.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Exponentiating the log modulus turns the zeta field into Boltzmann weights, with β acting as inverse temperature. The short-interval integral is therefore the direct thermodynamic bridge from critical-line values to a free energy.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Short-range and logarithmic models are separated by multiple observables: the logarithmic centering correction, the non-Gumbel density/tail, and a low-temperature free-energy plateau, allowing the hypothesis to be challenged at more than one representational level.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The reported tests are preliminary, converge slowly, omit lower-order arithmetic effects in places, and are not independent validation of the proposed law.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Testing both normalized maxima and the beta-dependent partition free energy probes the same freezing proposal through an extreme-value view and a phase-transition view rather than relying on a single fit.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The source provides numerical consistency only; figure extraction is incomplete and no claimed test is presented as conclusive.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Maximum statistics and thermodynamic behavior as complementary views

risk_spans.reason: Bibliography is interleaved with nonpropositional Figure 2 plotting symbols and coordinates; no additional mathematical argument is recoverable.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The freezing proposal becomes a shape prediction: normalized free energy should follow a temperature-dependent curve below the critical point and then flatten. The reported plateau supplies a phase-transition view complementary to the maximum statistics.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Using the zeta partition function, the source forms f(β)=-(β log N_T)^{-1}log z_β and averages it over many T values near a large height. Freezing predicts -f(β)=β+1/β for β<1 and the constant value 2 for β>1. After subtracting lower-order arithmetic terms, the plotted numerical results are reported as consistent with this breakpoint and plateau.
directed.conceptual_reading: A plateau means that increasing inverse temperature no longer changes the leading normalized free energy: the measure is already dominated by the deepest landscape values. This tests the same proposed mechanism through thermodynamic response rather than only through an extreme-value distribution.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The β-curve of normalized free energy is a compact representation of an entire family of zeta-weighted integrals. Its kink and flat low-temperature branch translate the statistical-mechanical notion of freezing into a directly comparable zeta observable.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Numerical consistency after a lower-order correction is not proof of a phase transition or of the zeta/freezing correspondence. The extracted figure lacks precise plotting data, and the subtraction introduces an additional modeling dependency.
directed.uncertainty: The qualitative critical point, high-temperature curve, plateau, and reported agreement are readable. Exact data values, normalization details, and the arithmetic renormalization require the original figure or scan.
